items.front: Constitutional vs statutory vs executive body — the source test?
items.back: Constitutional = named in the Constitution (ECI, CAG, UPSC, FC); Statutory = created by an Act (NHRC, CVC, Lokpal); Executive = by Cabinet resolution (NITI Aayog).
items.examPoint: Constitutional vs statutory vs executive bodies — distinction
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Constitutional bodies

items.front: ECI — Article, size and multi-member milestone?
items.back: Art 324; single-member from 1950; permanently multi-member (CEC + 2 ECs = 3) since Oct 1993. Size is NOT fixed by the Constitution.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Constitutional bodies

items.back: CEC removed only like a Supreme Court judge (impeachment); an EC/Regional Commissioner only on the CEC's recommendation. Term: 6 yrs or age 65.
items.examPoint: ECI — appointment, tenure & removal (CEC vs ECs independence)
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Constitutional bodies

items.front: CAG — Article, tenure, and India-vs-Britain contrast?
items.back: Art 148; 6 yrs or age 65; removed like an SC judge. India's CAG is only an Auditor (post-facto, no control over issue of money); Britain's is both Comptroller AND Auditor.
items.examPoint: CAG — duties, powers, audit reports & India-Britain contrast
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Constitutional bodies

items.front: CAG reports — how many, examined by whom?
items.back: Three reports (Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts, Public Undertakings); laid in legislature and examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC). CAG = 'friend, philosopher & guide' of PAC.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Constitutional bodies

items.back: 22 members = 15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha; 1-year term; chaired by convention by an Opposition member; examines the CAG's audit reports.
items.examPoint: PAC composition (22 = 15 LS + 7 RS) & scrutiny of CAG reports

items.front: Finance Commission — Article, cycle, composition, 16th FC?
items.back: Art 280; constituted by President every 5th year; Chairman + 4 members; advisory. 16th FC — Chair Arvind Panagariya, award period 2026-31.
items.examPoint: Finance Commission — Article 280, composition & functions (16th FC)
items.source: APPSC GK; 16th FC verified online Sep 2026

items.front: UPSC — Articles, appointment, removal for misbehaviour?
items.back: Arts 315-323; members appointed by President; removed for misbehaviour only after a Supreme Court inquiry (binding). Expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; advisory role.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Constitutional bodies

items.front: SPSC — the three contrasts with UPSC?
items.back: SPSC members appointed by the Governor; age limit 62 (UPSC 65); but removable only by the President (not the Governor). A Joint SPSC is statutory, not constitutional.
items.examPoint: SPSC — Governor's appointment, tenure & removal only by President
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Constitutional bodies

items.front: Attorney General — Article, right in Parliament, tenure?
items.back: Art 76; first law officer; Art 88 lets him speak/take part in either House but NOT vote; holds office during the President's pleasure (no fixed term); may do private practice (not against Govt).
items.examPoint: Attorney General & Advocate General — law officers (Art 76 & 165)

items.front: NCSC / NCST / NCBC — Articles and the amendments?
items.back: NCSC Art 338 & NCST Art 338A (split by 89th Amendment 2003); NCBC made constitutional by 102nd Amendment 2018 (Art 338B, with Art 342A). All now constitutional.
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Constitutional bodies

items.front: GST Council — Article, chair, and voting rule?
items.back: Art 279A (101st Amendment); chaired ex-officio by the Union Finance Minister; Centre = ⅓, all States = ⅔; every decision needs a ¾ weighted majority.
items.examPoint: GST Council — Article 279A (101st Amendment) composition & voting
items.source: APPSC GK — Indian Polity: Constitutional bodies

items.front: Which bodies do NOT find mention in the Constitution?
items.back: NITI Aayog (executive 2015), erstwhile Planning Commission, NDC, Zonal Councils (statutory, SRA 1956). Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities IS constitutional (Art 350B, 7th Amendment).
items.examPoint: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities — Article 350B (7th Amendment)

items.front: NDC — who constitutes it (and who is NOT a member)?
items.back: PM (head) + all Union Cabinet Ministers + CMs of all States + UT Administrators + NITI Aayog members. The Finance Commission Chairman is NOT a member.
items.examPoint: NDC composition (PM + Union Cabinet + CMs; not FC Chairman)

items.back: CEC Gyanesh Kumar (26th, since Feb 2025); CAG K. Sanjay Murthy (15th, Nov 2024); Attorney General R. Venkataramani (since Oct 2022). 16th FC — Arvind Panagariya.
